# Interport Logistics LLC

Interport Logistics LLC is a Transportation, Logistics, Supply Chain and Storage company. Interport International Logistics Provider offers warehousing, distribution, consulting, etc for industries like hardware, retail, pharma and more. Interport Logistics LLC employs 111 people and has an annual revenue of $33.5M, founded in 2000. Headquartered in Miami, Florida, United States. Its workforce is distributed across 6 countries (including Colombia, United States, Spain, El Salvador, and Italy).

## About

Interport Logistics LLC provides integrated transportation, warehousing, customs brokerage and international freight services, tailoring logistics solutions for manufacturers, importers, distributors, retailers and e-commerce clients with emphasis on speed, visibility, compliance and refrigerated cargo capabilities.

- [2026-09-15 · Posted · 3 reactions] [📘 Interport Education | Dangerous Goods (DG) Basics Dangerous Goods...](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/interport-logistics-llc_interporteducation-dangerousgoods-dg-activity-7505610256484327424-LEpy)
  > 📘 Interport Education | Dangerous Goods (DG) Basics
  >
  > Dangerous Goods compliance begins before cargo reaches the warehouse, airport, port, or carrier.
  >
  > Dangerous Goods are articles or substances capable of posing a risk to health, safety, property, or the environment during transportation. Because of those risks, their movement is subject to specific regulatory requirements.
  >
  > The transportation framework categorizes Dangerous Goods into nine hazard classes, ranging from explosives and flammable materials to corrosives, radioactive materials, and miscellaneous dangerous goods.
  >
  > But identifying DG is only the beginning.
  >
  > A compliant shipment may require:
  >
  > 1. Identification — Determine whether the product is regulated for transportation.
  >
  > 2. Classification — Establish the appropriate UN number, proper shipping name, hazard class/division, packing group when applicable, and other relevant classification information.
  >
  > 3. Packaging — Use packaging permitted for the specific commodity, quantity, and mode of transportation.
  >
  > 4. Marking & Labeling — Apply the required package markings, hazard labels, and handling marks.
  >
  > 5. Documentation — Prepare the required dangerous-goods transportation documentation accurately.
  >
  > 6. Trained Personnel — Personnel performing regulated DG functions must have the appropriate training for their responsibilities.
  >
  > Why does this matter?
  >
  > Incorrectly declared or improperly prepared Dangerous Goods can result in shipment rejection, delays, additional costs, regulatory penalties, and—most importantly—serious safety risks.
  >
  > Products that appear routine can sometimes present transportation hazards. Lithium batteries are a particularly important example, but aerosols, perfumes, paints, chemicals, fuels, and many other products may also be regulated depending on their specific characteristics and transportation conditions.
  >
  > Requirements also differ by transportation mode. Air cargo is governed by applicable aviation dangerous-goods rules, while ocean transportation follows maritime requirements, with additional national regulations potentially applying.
  >
  > 💡 The key takeaway: If you are uncertain whether a product is regulated, don't assume—verify before you ship.
  >
  > At Interport Logistics, we believe safe transportation begins with accurate information, proper preparation, and compliance throughout the supply chain.
  >
  > 🎓 Interport Education
  > Knowledge That Moves Supply Chains.
